name: Bitwise Orthogonality Disguise
description: Replaces the arithmetic product condition with a bitwise operation condition: `(u | v) * (u & v) == 0`. Since the allowed states are 1 (binary 01) and 2 (binary 10), their bitwise AND is 0 if and only if they are different. Because the footprint is strictly non-negative, a sum of 0 forces every edge to have different states. This completely masks the bipartite/2-coloring requirement behind bitwise logic, defeating models that rely on algebraic or parity-based clues.
